subject: Eval readiness + small-sample scoring plan (Jupiter Health)
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@jupiterhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Eval readiness + small-sample scoring plan (Jupiter Health)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great to meet you both earlier. Quick recap and a proposed minimal plan to get the pilot eval running on Redwood so we can validate model fit within 1–2 weeks: 

1) Small-sample dataset: you mentioned ~500 de-identified outpatient triage exchanges. A CSV with columns: id, conversation_text, expected_intent, sensitive_flag (yes/no) is sufficient for the initial run. I attached a template.

2) Prompt sets & evaluator instructions: we suggest a 3-tier prompt set (happy-path, ambiguous, edge-case) — I attached the prompt file (jupiter_prompt_set_v1.txt). For scoring, we recommend: exact-intent match (binary), top-3 relevance (0-2), and a short free-text error tag.

3) Recommended models: start with Llama-3 13B quantized for a speed/cost baseline and try a 70B fp16 variant for quality checks on the same prompt set. We'll run both to compare latency, cost, and scoring metrics.

4) Quality regression & monitoring: include a small holdout (50 examples) that we keep constant across model updates. We'll surface automated regression alerts if intent accuracy drops >3% vs baseline.

5) Next steps / timeline:
- You upload the CSV to the Drive link I shared by Mon 4/26.
- Redwood runs the small-sample eval (both models) and returns a scorecard + per-example tags within 48 hours of receiving the dataset.
- 30-minute sync to review results — propose Wed 4/28 10:00am PT.

Attachments: jupiter_sample_dataset_template.csv (CSV template), jupiter_prompt_set_v1.txt (prompt set).

If that plan looks good I can kick off the eval queue as soon as the dataset is uploaded.

Thanks,
Mina

From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@jupiterhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Eval readiness + small-sample scoring plan (Jupiter Health)

Thanks Mina — this is clear and helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we prepare the dataset: 

- For the expected_intent column, do you have a preferred taxonomy? We can map to our current 12 intents, but wondering if you prefer a condensed set for the pilot.
- Are there any PII hashing requirements for the text column beyond de-identification? We can pseudonymize patient names/IDs.

Also, on the model choices: what trade-offs should we expect between the 13B quantized and 70B fp16 in terms of accuracy delta for intent detection? If it's typically marginal, we might prioritize the smaller model for cost.

We should be able to upload the CSV by Tue 4/27 EOD. Wed 4/28 10am PT works for the sync.

—Alex

alex.kim@jupiterhealth.com | (212) 555-8976

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@jupiterhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Eval readiness + small-sample scoring plan (Jupiter Health)

Alex — great questions. Answers below and a couple of pro tips for faster iteration: 

- Intent taxonomy: use your existing 12 intents for now. For the pilot we will map to a normalized set (we call it intent_v1) on our side so we can compare across customers later. Please send the intent list as an extra column (intent_source) if possible.

- PII hashing: pseudonymization is fine. For free-text fields we ask that PHI be redacted or replaced with tokens (e.g., [PATIENT_NAME]). No additional KMS wrapping needed for the pilot upload; if you move to Private deployment later we can enforce HSM + customer KMS.

- Model trade-offs: in our experience the 13B quantized gives 70–85% of the 70B's intent accuracy for straightforward intent detection tasks while being ~3–4x cheaper/token and ~2–3x lower latency. The 70B helps on ambiguous edge-cases and complex instruction-following. For this pilot, run both: use the 13B to validate throughput and cost; use the 70B on the holdout to benchmark quality headroom.

Operational notes: 
- Scoring rubric:
  * intent_match: 1/0 (binary)
  * relevance_rank: 0–2 (0 = irrelevant, 1 = partially, 2 = correct top rank)
  * error_tags: comma-separated short codes (e.g., MISINTENT, HALLUCINATION, TRUNCATION)
  * scorer_notes: free text (optional)

- File upload: please put the CSV in the Drive folder (link below) and notify me. We will not start processing until we confirm column parity.

Drive: https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/1a2b3c/jupiter-eval-specs

I'll queue the eval run once the CSV is uploaded. Ben — looping you in for any commercial questions / scheduling.

Cheers,
Mina
